text.title: Cohort Implementation Core Rules
text.summary: 9 testable rules every Cohort Implementation application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: `cohort_week` MUST be the signup timestamp converted to UTC and truncated to the week starting Monday (`DATE_TRUNC(DATE(signup_ts_utc), WEEK(MONDAY))` on BigQuery or the engine's equivalent). Every timestamp column the model reads MUST be UTC; local-time columns MUST NOT be used for cohort assignment.

rationale.source: templates/cohort-retention-weekly.sql; BigQuery DATE_TRUNC and Snowflake WEEK_START documentation

rule.rationale: Engines default the week start differently (Sunday on BigQuery, session-dependent on Snowflake), and a signup at 23:30 local on Sunday lands in a different cohort depending on the column used. Two dashboards built from the same table then disagree about which week a user belongs to.

rule.statement: Cohort membership and retention events MUST join on a stable, post-identification `user_id`. Anonymous `distinct_id`, device id, or cookie id MUST NOT appear in the model; identity resolution MUST happen upstream in `stg_users` / `stg_events` before this model reads them.

rationale.source: AGENTS.md scope: stable user_id in events, not anonymous distinct_id; Mixpanel and Amplitude identity-management documentation

rule.rationale: A user who signs up on mobile and returns on desktop is two anonymous ids and zero retained users. Cohorts built on device ids under-report retention by exactly the share of multi-device users, and the number moves whenever the app's identity-merge behaviour changes.

rule.statement: The retention event (e.g. `event_type = 'login'`) MUST be declared in exactly one place in the model, named in the model's `schema.yml` description, and recorded in the artefact's `settings.retention_event`. Changing it MUST be treated as a new model version with a full historical backfill; an in-place change without backfill MUST be rejected.

rationale.source: templates/schema.yml; dbt documentation on model contracts and incremental backfills

rule.rationale: An incremental model that switches from `login` to `session_start` mid-history carries old cohorts on one definition and new cohorts on another, and the retention curve shows a step change on the deploy date that gets investigated as a product event.

rule.statement: `day_offset` MUST be restricted to the fixed set the config declares (the template uses 1, 7, 14, 30, 60, 90), enforced both in the model's `WHERE` clause and by a dbt `accepted_values` test in `schema.yml`. Ad-hoc offsets MUST NOT be added by editing a query in a BI tool.

rationale.source: templates/schema.yml accepted_values test; dbt tests documentation

rule.rationale: Offsets that exist only in a dashboard query drift from the model and cannot be backfilled. The test turns a silent divergence into a failed build.

rule.statement: An event MUST count toward retention only when `event_ts_utc >= signup_ts_utc` and the offset is computed as whole days between the two dates. Events before signup (imports, pre-registration activity) MUST be excluded by the join condition, not by a later filter.
rule.rationale: Backfilled or migrated users carry events dated before their signup row. Without the guard they appear at a negative offset, or worse, at day 0 of a later cohort, and the day-1 retention of migration weeks spikes.

rule.statement: Retention for a `(cohort_week, day_offset)` cell MUST be computed as distinct users with a qualifying event at that offset divided by distinct users in the cohort at signup. The denominator MUST come from the users table, not from the count of rows in the long-format model, and MUST NOT shrink to "users seen at day 1".

rationale.source: Lean Analytics (Croll and Yoskovitz); Amplitude retention-analysis documentation

rule.rationale: The long-format model only contains retained users, so counting its rows as the denominator yields 100 percent retention at every offset. Conditioning on day-1 activity produces a flattering "bounded" retention that hides the largest drop.

rule.statement: A cell MUST be reported only when `cohort_week + 6 days + day_offset` is on or before the data cutoff date. Cells that have not matured MUST be null in the chart spec, never zero, and the chart MUST render them as blank.

rationale.source: widely established cohort-analysis practice (the incomplete lower-right triangle)

rule.rationale: Immature cells rendered as zero draw the retention curve plunging for the newest cohorts every week. Teams that have not seen this before open an incident; teams that have learn to ignore the chart, which is worse.

rule.statement: The model MUST be materialised as incremental with `unique_key = [cohort_week, day_offset, user_id]`, partitioned on `cohort_week`, and its incremental filter MUST look back at least as far as the largest `day_offset` (90 days in the template) so late events for older cohorts are captured. `not_null` tests MUST exist on all three key columns.

rationale.source: templates/cohort-retention-weekly.sql; dbt incremental models documentation (unique_key, is_incremental)

rule.rationale: A lookback shorter than the largest offset means a user's day-90 event never lands, because their cohort left the incremental window weeks ago; day-90 retention then decays toward zero for every cohort older than the lookback. The composite key is what makes re-runs idempotent.

rule.statement: The `settings` object of the config artefact MUST declare `warehouse_engine` (one of `bigquery`, `snowflake`, `postgres`, `redshift`), `retention_event`, `day_offsets` (the list from the model), `week_start` (`monday`) and `timezone` (`UTC`). Values MUST match the deployed SQL and `schema.yml`; a mismatch MUST fail review.
rule.rationale: The config is the only thing a downstream chart or a second analyst reads without opening the SQL. If it does not carry the engine, event and offsets, the chart is built on assumptions that the SQL does not share.
